pages.title: Build a Nixflex integration
pages.lead: Build an integration by verifying one authenticated read, then adding a workflow whose results you can track.
important: Keep the account credential on your server and match it to the intended API host.
Record a write before sending it; a lost response may conceal success.
Use the task guides below and the API reference for exact fields.

pages.title: Authenticate API requests securely
pages.lead: Authenticate server requests with the full account credential and keep personal team access separate from API authority.
important: Send both key parts in the Bearer header; never put the credential in a browser bundle.
The shared account key is not a restricted Member credential.
API-key rotation and webhook signing-secret rotation are separate actions.

pages.title: Handle API errors in code
pages.lead: Use the HTTP status and machine error code to choose between correcting input, retrying a read and reconciling a write.
important: Branch on error.code, not the wording of error.message.
An error or lost connection can leave a write outcome unknown.
Keep a non-JSON error fallback and log only safe diagnostic fields.

pages.title: Build reliable paginated API reads
pages.lead: Build a list adapter for each endpoint’s paging shape, preserving its account, filters and progress until the scan finishes.
important: There is no universal page parameter or list envelope.
Reject repeated cursors and bound long scans.
Store progress after processing a page; concurrent changes can shift offset rows.
pages.description: Read Nixflex cursor and offset lists without changing their filters, losing message ties or treating an offset scan as a stable snapshot.

pages.title: Pace API requests and polling
pages.lead: Use response headers and a bounded polling policy to stay within the account’s current API request allowance.
important: Honour Retry-After for a safe read and stop at an application deadline.
HTTP request quotas, call capacity and feature limits are different.
A throttle does not grant permission to repeat an uncertain write.

pages.title: Prevent duplicate work in code
pages.lead: Persist each intended operation before sending it and use the identity mechanism supported by that specific endpoint.
important: A call request UUID is not the same as a Knowledge Idempotency-Key header.
Keep the original account, API base URL, identity and exact input while reconciling.
A new identity represents a new action and can create duplicate work.
pages.description: Save outbound call UUIDs and Knowledge operation keys correctly, keep their account and environment binding, and reconcile other uncertain writes.

pages.title: Build an agent knowledge workflow
pages.lead: Build an agent knowledge workflow from source preparation through reviewed publication and tested answers.
important: Each agent owns one base shared by its attached numbers.
Request review explicitly; accepted preparation is not confirmed publication.
Keep base, source, draft, topic and job IDs distinct.
pages.description: Choose the right knowledge task: ingest sources, review facts, test answers, maintain exports or manage agent keyterms.

pages.title: Build a single outbound call
pages.lead: Create one authorised outbound call with a specific purpose, then reconcile its request and call results without automatic redial.
important: Creating the request can place a real call and incur charges.
Save a UUID with the exact account, base URL and call inputs before the first send.
An accepted request, a completed call and a confirmed booking are different results.

pages.title: Build a voice campaign workflow
pages.lead: Prepare a voice campaign’s recipients and permission checks, create executable work, then track that same campaign through its results.
important: Campaign creation can launch immediately or run when its schedule is due.
A duplicate warning is not a sending lock; choose the required policy deliberately.
Cancel stops future dispatch and does not hang up active calls.

pages.title: Apply recipient contact controls
pages.lead: Preview recipient-local contact hours and enforce suppression decisions before requesting calls or messages.
important: A preview sends nothing and does not authorise later dispatch.
Use known recipient location; do not substitute the business time zone.
Recipient opt-outs remain enforced and cannot be removed as business entries.

pages.title: Manage phone number settings in code
pages.lead: Read an owned number, change only its intended settings and verify the result without recreating its connections.
important: URL-encode the number, including the leading plus sign.
Moving an owned number preserves number-owned settings but changes inherited agent behaviour.
Null means inherit only on fields that explicitly document it.

pages.title: Build team administration in code
pages.lead: Build team administration from the current organisation context, role rules and invitation state.
important: People use personal logins; a shared API key has account authority.
Admins manage Members, while ownership and Admin changes require the Owner.
Ownership acceptance and account closure use the person’s dashboard flow.

pages.title: Build an inbox for SMS and web conversations
pages.lead: Read a number’s SMS or website threads, preserve server paging and mark only the messages the user actually saw as read.
important: Check feature availability before rendering an empty inbox.
Preserve read_version as a decimal string and pair both message cursor fields.
Archiving does not delete messages or turn off automatic replies.

pages.title: Read usage and plan call capacity
pages.lead: Read the account’s usage and capacity without treating counters as invoices or a promise that the next call will start.
important: Null or absent values mean unknown, not zero.
Call capacity and HTTP request limits are separate.
Payments and saved payment methods use the permitted dashboard workflow.

pages.title: Send one SMS with the API
pages.lead: Send one requested message from an explicit owned sender and retain the acceptance result without assuming delivery.
important: This request can contact a real recipient; it has no dry-run mode.
Use to for the recipient and from_number for the owned sender.
Do not resend an unknown outcome or bypass a do_not_contact refusal.

pages.title: Configure automatic SMS replies
pages.lead: Give an owned number SMS-specific instructions, enable replies deliberately and check the resulting conversations.
important: Telephone instructions and the SMS prompt are separate.
Archiving a thread does not disable replies.
Knowledge and calendar actions need their own enabled channel or connection.

pages.title: Build an SMS campaign workflow
pages.lead: Prepare an SMS campaign’s template, recipients and contact checks, then track acceptance, delivery and replies separately.
important: Creating a campaign can send immediately or when scheduled.
SMS creation makes new work; it has no reuse_campaign_id replacement mode.
Keep uncertain sends visible and reconcile the saved campaign ID.

pages.title: Configure post-call SMS follow-ups
pages.lead: Configure a permitted text after a telephone call using a usable template and the number’s actual origin rules.
important: Post-call SMS is separate from in-call SMS, replies and a direct send.
API-origin numbers do not automatically inherit the agent enable switch.
Avoid sending the same follow-up again from your webhook handler.

pages.title: Configure website chat and voice in code
pages.lead: Manage a number’s website settings with revision checks, then verify the dashboard-generated installation on the real site.
important: Never give the browser the account API credential.
Website voice needs both the Web agent and voice switches enabled.
Public visitor details are unverified, and enabled custom functions must be safe for them.

pages.title: Configure SMS during a phone call
pages.lead: Allow the phone agent to send a useful text during a conversation only when the in-call SMS switch and recipient checks permit it.
important: Prompt wording does not bypass a disabled SMS action.
In-call texts, post-call texts and SMS replies use separate controls.
A send acceptance must not be presented as confirmed handset delivery.

pages.title: Configure call endings and timers
pages.lead: Configure silence and duration limits alongside clear instructions for ending a completed conversation.
important: Silence timeout and maximum call duration serve different purposes.
func_end_call:false disables those timers, not every model-requested hangup.
A client polling timeout does not end the telephone call.

pages.title: Let a caller ask the agent to wait
pages.lead: Use the prompt-enabled wait action when a telephone caller needs time, while preserving the call’s other limits.
important: Enable the behaviour in the instructions that the current call uses.
Waiting does not remove the maximum duration or other end conditions.
Website voice does not use this telephone WAIT action.

pages.title: Configure outbound phone-menu waiting
pages.lead: Configure bounded waiting while an outbound call navigates a phone menu and listens for a human.
important: The menu wait limit is separate from caller silence and call duration.
Use clear routing instructions and test the actual menu.
This is an outbound telephone behaviour, not website navigation.

pages.title: Configure a human call handoff
pages.lead: Configure cold or warm transfer and report a successful handoff only after the transfer result confirms it.
important: Use an eligible destination and the intended transfer type.
Warm transfer can use a whisper; cold transfer follows a different path.
A transfer request alone does not prove a human answered.

pages.title: Connect call instructions to actions
pages.lead: Connect a phone agent’s instructions to configured actions and use each action’s result to decide what the agent may confirm.
important: A prompt cannot grant an action that its switch or connection blocks.
Verify booking, sending and transfer results before claiming success.
Website visitors have a different action boundary from telephone callers.

pages.title: Connect Cal.com bookings in code
pages.lead: Connect Cal.com to an owned number, choose the intended event settings and verify booking results before confirming an appointment.
important: Calendar access and the agent’s permission to act are separate.
Confirm the spoken name and email independently before booking.
Use returned booking results; an accepted action is not proof of notification delivery.

pages.title: Send call results to Slack
pages.lead: Connect an owned number’s Slack notification settings and test the result with approved call data.
important: Keep connection credentials and private workspace data on the server.
A saved connection is not proof that every future notification will arrive.
Reconcile an uncertain update before changing the same connection again.

pages.title: Connect call results to GoHighLevel
pages.lead: Connect the intended GoHighLevel workspace to an owned number and check the resulting contact or call update.
important: Use the exact workspace and permissions required by the saved connection.
Connection success and a later business update are separate results.
Keep uncertain outcomes visible instead of creating duplicate records.

pages.title: Build event automations with Zapier or Make
pages.lead: Receive Nixflex events in an automation workflow that authenticates deliveries and avoids repeating business actions.
important: Verify the original delivery bytes before trusting event data.
Acknowledge only after durable acceptance, then process asynchronously.
Use event-specific duplicate keys; do not treat every event as one completed call.

pages.title: Choose an integration workflow
pages.lead: Choose the connection or event workflow that matches the business task, its permissions and its recovery requirements.
important: Use a calendar connection for booking and signed events for downstream processing.
Number connections and account-wide services have different scopes.
Confirm the result in the destination before presenting work as complete.

pages.title: Prepare a phone number connection
pages.lead: Prepare an owned carrier number for Nixflex with the correct credentials, agent assignment and routing checks.
important: Import connects an existing eligible number; it is not a number purchase or port.
Credentials stay private and must match the selected carrier and account.
An uncertain routing result needs reconciliation before another import.

pages.title: Connect an agent to your business API
pages.lead: Expose a narrowly scoped business function to an agent and treat its response as the authority for whether the action succeeded.
important: Describe exact arguments and validate them in your service.
Public website access requires all enabled number functions to be safe for visitors.
A timeout can follow a successful business write; reconcile before repeating it.

pages.title: Provide context before an inbound call
pages.lead: Use the pre-call hook to supply temporary context or an explicit rejection before an eligible inbound conversation.
important: Hook failure is fail-open; do not use it as the sole security boundary.
Verify signatures over the exact request bytes.
The outbound call purpose is supplied on the call request, not through this hook.

pages.title: Configure recording and private playback
pages.lead: Configure the effective recording decision and use authenticated recording access to check whether audio is actually available.
important: A number’s explicit recording value overrides the agent, including false and true.
Changing settings affects new work and does not erase old audio.
An absent URL or pending recording is not proof that no copy exists.

pages.title: Configure telephone keypad input
pages.lead: Enable the number-aware keypad setting when a telephone workflow needs digits and verify the captured result.
important: Number overrides and the agent setting determine effective keypad access.
Website chat and voice do not gain telephone keypad actions.
Validate received digits before using them for a business action.

pages.title: Configure outbound voicemail behaviour
pages.lead: Configure machine detection and a brief voicemail message for outbound calls without assuming a message will always be left.
important: API-origin and dashboard-origin numbers select message settings differently.
Carrier machine detection can end the call before the leave-message path.
Detected voicemail skips automatic post-call SMS.

pages.title: Extract structured facts after a call
pages.lead: Define the facts your application needs after a call and preserve incomplete or unavailable analysis until processing finishes.
important: A completed call can still have unfinished post-call work.
Extracted facts are model output; validate them before consequential actions.
Use structured fields and signed results rather than parsing a summary as a receipt.

pages.title: Connect a compatible model account
pages.lead: Connect an authorised compatible model account and test its actual conversation behaviour before using it with customers.
important: Use the supported connection flow and keep the provider credential private.
Saving a connection does not prove every later request will succeed.
Account connection settings and the legacy agent llm_model field are different.

pages.title: Use a voice from your own provider account
pages.lead: Use a voice from your own provider account by connecting its authorised key and voice identifier through the supported account settings.
important: The voice already belongs to your provider account; supply its existing identifier.
Keep the provider key private and verify the connection before using it on calls.
A later failure can use a fallback path, so test actual speech and charges.

pages.title: Store recordings in your own bucket
pages.lead: Connect your own compatible storage bucket and verify the private recording object, playback and cleanup behaviour.
important: Connection verification and a later recording upload are separate results.
Keep bucket credentials and playback access private.
Automatic Nixflex retention does not remove your own bucket’s copies.

pages.title: Write clear agent instructions
pages.lead: Write instructions that state the task, essential facts and action boundaries, then test both normal and uncertain conversations.
important: Use one question at a time and confirm consequential names, dates and contact details.
Put longer business facts in knowledge instead of repeating them in every prompt.
Instructions do not bypass disabled actions or grant permissions.

pages.title: Write reliable phone-menu instructions
pages.lead: Describe the intended department and exit conditions so an outbound agent can navigate and test a real phone menu.
important: Test the current menu rather than relying on an old digit sequence.
Keep menu waiting bounded and explain what to do when the route fails.
An answered menu is not a completed human handoff.

pages.title: Understand how agent knowledge is used
pages.lead: Agent knowledge supplies reviewed facts to enabled channels without granting permission to take actions.
important: One agent owns the base shared by its attached numbers.
Small bases can supply all topics; Test evidence is supplied context, not an accuracy score.
A source, draft, publication job and live topic represent different stages.

pages.title: Understand settings across agent channels
pages.lead: Choose settings for the channel that actually uses them; a saved field does not have the same effect on every conversation.
important: Phone, SMS and website instructions are separate.
Website visitors have a narrower built-in action set.
Compatibility fields may be stored without controlling current runtime behaviour.

pages.title: Resolve number overrides and agent defaults
pages.lead: Resolve each effective setting using its documented number, agent and channel rules rather than one universal inheritance rule.
important: An explicit number recording value wins over the agent.
Caller memory and name greetings are independent controls.
New-agent retention is inherited once; later default changes are not bulk edits.

pages.title: Understand retention and saved copies
pages.lead: Set call and message retention while keeping policy eligibility, completed cleanup and customer-owned copies distinct.
important: New agents inherit the account default; existing agents keep their saved policy.
A saved policy or elapsed time does not prove cleanup completed.
Apply separate retention to your bucket, downloads and webhook storage.

pages.title: Choose voices and speaking settings
pages.lead: Choose an eligible catalog voice and verify the actual spoken result for the intended channel and language.
important: Use the current catalog key instead of a hard-coded display-name list.
speaking_rate affects speed; legacy voice_speed does not.
Fallback can change the voice heard even when configuration was saved.

pages.title: Understand agents and number ownership
pages.lead: Use an agent for shared conversation behaviour and knowledge, with phone numbers carrying their own channels and connections.
important: Separate agents when branches need different knowledge.
Moving a number changes inherited behaviour while number-owned settings remain.
Deleting an agent switches it off; it does not erase history or detach numbers.

pages.title: Understand caller memory and greetings
pages.lead: Use saved caller context to continue a telephone conversation while treating it as information to confirm, not verified identity.
important: Memory and a saved-name greeting are separate switches.
Call retention does not erase every caller or visitor record.
Explicit caller-context updates and website visitor cards have separate scopes.

pages.title: Understand organisation roles and credentials
pages.lead: Keep shared organisation work separate from personal membership, role permissions and the account API credential.
important: Owner, Admin and Member permissions are enforced by the server.
A shared API key does not inherit the restricted role of the person holding it.
Ownership offers and account closure require personal dashboard actions.

pages.title: Understand phone number ownership and scope
pages.lead: Treat a phone number as an owned connection with its own settings and one current attached agent.
important: Import origin is provenance, not a writable permission switch.
A move preserves number-owned data while changing inherited agent behaviour.
Removal from Nixflex does not imply external number rental has ended.

pages.title: Understand inbound call admission and results
pages.lead: Follow an inbound call from account and number admission checks through conversation actions and later results.
important: A connected number does not guarantee every call will be answered.
The pre-call hook is fail-open and cannot be the only security boundary.
Call completion does not prove recording, messages or event delivery succeeded.

pages.title: Understand outbound requests and call outcomes
pages.lead: Treat an outbound call as an authorised request with a specific purpose, a saved identity and results that arrive in separate stages.
important: A purpose is required and is not permission to contact a recipient.
Save request_id before sending and keep its original account and base URL.
Acceptance, completion and a booking result are different states.

pages.title: Choose language and recognition settings
pages.lead: Choose a supported speech language for the selected voice route and test the names and phrases your callers use.
important: A prompt cannot add language support missing from a speech route.
Recognition hints do not control pronunciation or guarantee a transcript.
A written chat test does not validate live speech behaviour.

pages.title: Understand live monitoring and takeover
pages.lead: Let authorised teammates listen to eligible active calls and distinguish a requested takeover from a committed human handoff.
important: Eligible Members can use Listen and takeover without becoming general writers.
After committed takeover the AI does not return automatically.
An accepted End request is not proof the connection has ended.

pages.title: Understand authenticated live listening
pages.lead: Use the supported authenticated session flow to listen to an eligible call without exposing the shared account key to the browser.
important: Media access is scoped and short-lived.
Listening and speaking through a committed takeover are different states.
Expiry, call completion and permission changes can end audio access.

pages.title: Understand website voice permissions
pages.lead: Enable website voice through the installed widget while preserving the number’s website settings and public-visitor boundaries.
important: Both web_agent_enabled and web_calls_enabled must permit voice.
Visitor contact details are self-reported, not verified identity.
Website functions do not unlock built-in telephone booking, SMS or transfer actions.

pages.title: Understand conversation controls and actions
pages.lead: Combine clear turn-taking instructions with the effective action switches, timers and actual conversation results.
important: A prompt cannot guarantee timing or enable a disabled action.
Waiting, silence handling and call duration are separate controls.
Confirm actions only after their results succeed.

pages.title: Use dynamic variables without guessing data
pages.lead: Insert known application data into the correct call or message template and reject missing consequential values before sending work.
important: Single calls use dynamic_vars; campaign rows use nested variables.
Template syntax varies by field and must be checked against its contract.
Caller-supplied contact details are data, not proof of identity.

pages.title: Debug failed requests safely
pages.lead: Investigate a failed request using its status, machine code and safe diagnostic identifier before deciding whether any action should be repeated.
important: A response can be missing, incomplete or non-JSON; keep a fallback parser.
A 2xx response can accept background work without completing it.
Never replay a copied write merely to reproduce an error.
pages.description: Investigate Nixflex API failures using safe request identifiers and machine codes, while preserving unknown write outcomes and non-JSON errors.

pages.title: Understand API quotas and call capacity
pages.lead: Plan HTTP requests and business work against their separate current limits instead of assuming one fixed allowance.
important: Read rate headers and current max_concurrent; neither is a universal throughput promise.
A successful usage read does not reserve a call slot.
A throttle does not make an uncertain write safe to repeat.
pages.description: Separate Nixflex HTTP request allowances, concurrent calls, messaging capacity and Knowledge limits, then handle each refusal using its actual result.

pages.title: Use the Node SDK in a server application
pages.description: Install the reviewed Node SDK candidate, make a safe read, persist outbound call intent and reconcile typed results without automatic mutation retries.
pages.lead: Use the Node SDK for server-side reads and deliberate writes, with durable outbound request records for uncertain call outcomes.
important: Keep the complete account credential on the server and supply the intended base URL.
Install the exact reviewed 0.11.0 candidate; the version alone is not its identity.
Prepare and save a call locally before a separately approved send.

pages.title: Use the Python SDK with sync or async code
pages.description: Install the reviewed Python candidate, manage sync and async clients, save outbound request IDs and preserve unknown write and booking states.
pages.lead: Use the Python SDK with a managed synchronous or asynchronous client, keeping reads, approved writes and recovery separate.
important: The reviewed 0.4.0 package requires Python 3.9 or later and httpx.
Automatic retries are GET-only; a failed mutation can still have happened.
Local call preparation stays synchronous even on AsyncNixflex.

pages.title: Call the API from another language
pages.description: Use direct HTTPS with private bearer credentials, bounded reads and schema-aware error handling, then verify generated clients against the public contract.
pages.lead: Use standard HTTPS from any server language, following the public contract and explicit retry rules for each operation.
important: Send the complete bearer credential only to the intended API host.
A timeout or malformed write response can hide success; do not automatically replay it.
A generated client does not add missing idempotency, privacy or business-result checks.

pages.title: Choose an API client or developer tool
pages.description: Compare the reviewed Node, Python, CLI and MCP candidates, check exact package identity and choose HTTP when a client method is not verified.
pages.lead: Choose a client for your application, then verify the exact reviewed package before relying on its methods.
important: The reviewed packages are unpublished candidates; a registry install does not prove that they are available.
The same version number can identify different candidate archives, so check the release hash.
Use the public HTTP contract when a client method is not verified.

pages.title: Use the CLI with a private account connection
pages.description: Install the reviewed CLI, choose the account and API host explicitly, understand private input and distinguish read retries from deliberate writes.
pages.lead: Use the CLI for explicit terminal operations with a private credential, a known API host and checked command results.
important: The CLI ships in the reviewed Node package and needs Node 18 or later.
Pass the intended base URL explicitly; NIXFLEX_BASE_URL alone is not the legacy CLI’s host selector.
A command can perform a write without a confirmation flag, so read its contract before running it.

pages.title: Make a safe CLI read and prepare a call
pages.description: Verify the CLI account connection with a usage read, prepare an outbound UUID locally and keep any approved send separate from read-only recovery.
pages.lead: Verify the CLI with one safe read, then prepare a recoverable call intention locally before deciding whether to send it.
important: The first request reads usage and does not create an account, call or message.
Use --output for prepared JSON; do not rely on PowerShell redirection encoding.
Never put preparation and sending inside an automatic retry loop.

pages.title: Find the CLI command for your task
pages.description: Find reviewed CLI command families, exact call recovery commands, private credential inputs and confirmation boundaries before running a change.
pages.lead: Choose the command for one task and read its effect, required inputs and recovery rule before execution.
important: Use the exact reviewed candidate and explicit --base-url for your account.
A confirmation preview is command-specific; creates can send immediately.
Use private input for secrets and keep JSON results out of shared logs.

pages.title: Add knowledge sources through the API
pages.description: Create an agent knowledge base, submit text or files for review, and discover website pages without mistaking preparation for publication.
pages.lead: Prepare text, files or selected website pages for an agent’s knowledge base, with review requested before new facts become live.
important: Create one knowledge base for the agent, not for each number.
Save the operation key and returned job ID before starting another import.
Set review:true explicitly; the API default can publish after preparation.

pages.title: Review and publish knowledge drafts
pages.description: Inspect prepared facts, save draft edits with current revisions, approve selected topics and confirm the publication job before using new answers.
pages.lead: Turn a prepared knowledge draft into live answers by reviewing its facts, choosing topics and confirming publication.
important: A prepared source is not the same as published knowledge.
Use the latest base revision and draft edit revision for each save or acceptance.
Warnings and flagged topics need explicit human choices.

pages.title: Test and troubleshoot knowledge answers
pages.description: Run an agent knowledge-only test, inspect supplied topic evidence and resolve missing, stale or loading answers without placing calls or sending messages.
pages.lead: Test whether an agent can answer from its published knowledge, then use the returned evidence to fix missing or stale facts.
important: Knowledge tests use live unsuppressed facts and perform no call, booking or message action.
Evidence shows supplied context; it does not prove every listed topic shaped the answer.
A full call test is a separate step for agent instructions, speech and actions.

pages.title: Refresh and export agent knowledge
pages.description: Maintain saved knowledge sources, preserve reviewed changes and download a revision-bound export while handling stale jobs and cleanup safely.
pages.lead: Refresh saved source material deliberately and export a known knowledge revision without losing reviewed changes.
important: A website source changes only when you request and review the appropriate refresh.
Deleting a topic prevents that same saved source from recreating it on refresh.
Exports expire after one hour and become stale when the base revision changes.

pages.title: Read and manage agent keyterms
pages.description: Read automatic knowledge hints and saved manual keyterms, respect the returned limits and update only the writable manual agent field.
pages.lead: Read the speaking hints derived from an agent’s knowledge and manage the separate manual keyterms you choose.
important: Automatic knowledge_keyterms are read-only and do not consume the manual allowance.
Write manual terms through boosted_keywords on the agent.
Use the returned limits; dashboard chips can differ from the raw saved API lists.

pages.title: Choose webhook events for your integration
pages.description: Choose call, booking and SMS events by what they prove, and keep pre-call callbacks, custom functions and unsigned reachability tests separate.
pages.lead: Choose the event that proves the business result you need, then process it using its own identity and delivery rules.
important: Call completion does not prove final analysis, recording access or a booking result.
Use call.bookings for confirmed post-call calendar mutations and reconcile its final state.
Unsigned test traffic must never trigger business actions.

pages.title: Recover delayed or repeated webhook deliveries
pages.description: Handle webhook timing, retries, duplicates and missed events with durable acceptance and authenticated reads instead of repeating calls or bookings.
pages.lead: Recover delayed, repeated or missing webhook deliveries by reconciling saved work with authenticated resource reads.
important: Save verified events durably before returning 2xx.
Use an atomic deduplication key and a separate durable processing queue.
Delivery timing is not a deadline or a guarantee that an event will arrive.

pages.title: Manage team invitations and role changes
pages.description: Build team administration with personal role checks, invitation expiry and seat limits, while preserving unknown invitation and removal outcomes.
pages.lead: Invite people and manage permitted roles from the current organisation context, keeping personal access separate from the shared server key.
important: Admins manage Members; Admin and ownership changes require the Owner.
Pending unexpired invitations count towards seats.
A person’s role restriction must never be bypassed with a shared key in the browser.

pages.title: Handle ownership changes and account closure
pages.description: Keep ownership acceptance, leaving and account closure in the authenticated personal flow, and reconcile access, key handling and unfinished work.
pages.lead: Direct ownership and closure decisions through the authorised person’s dashboard flow, then reconcile the resulting access in your integration.
important: Ownership acceptance and account closure require a personal authenticated flow.
Never invent public transfer or closure endpoints from dashboard behaviour.
A removed membership does not revoke a separately shared server key.

pages.title: Prepare and launch a voice campaign
pages.description: Validate voice campaign recipients, consent, local hours and duplicate policy before creating executable campaign work once.
pages.lead: Prepare a voice campaign as executable work: validate recipients and sending choices before creating it.
important: Default now mode requests launch immediately; scheduled work can launch when due.
Duplicate warnings do not block dispatch or provide request idempotency.
Save campaign_id even when creation succeeds but launch is refused or uncertain.

pages.title: Track voice campaign results and controls
pages.description: Read voice campaign state, resolve holds and cancel or resume unsent work while keeping queued calls, connected calls and final outcomes distinct.
pages.lead: Track the saved voice campaign and control future dispatch without recreating recipients whose outcomes are uncertain.
important: Queued work and the legacy dialed count do not prove a connected call.
Cancel stops future dispatch; it does not hang up active calls.
Resume operates on the existing campaign and does not mean repeat completed recipients.

pages.title: Prepare and send an SMS campaign
pages.description: Build SMS campaign templates and recipient variables, review consent and hours, and create one campaign while preserving uncertain outcomes.
pages.lead: Prepare a complete SMS template and recipient set, then create the campaign once with explicit contact choices.
important: Creating a campaign can send immediately or automatically when scheduled.
Every template placeholder needs a value in each recipient’s nested variables.
SMS creation always creates new work; reuse_campaign_id is not supported.

pages.title: Read SMS campaign delivery and controls
pages.description: Track SMS sent, delivered, failed and reply counts separately, cancel unsent work and reconcile uncertain sends without creating duplicate campaigns.
pages.lead: Track the existing SMS campaign’s delivery and reply evidence, then control only the work that remains eligible to send.
important: Sent, delivered, failed and reply counts describe different outcomes.
Cancel stops future dispatch and cannot recall a message already sent.
Deletion guidance is pending the final B57 contract; do not infer it from cancellation.

pages.title: Import and connect an owned phone number
pages.description: Prepare a supported number connection, use the dashboard for new imports and verify saved state and routing without exposing private credentials.
pages.lead: Connect an existing eligible number to an active owned agent, then verify both the saved number and its routing outcome.
important: Import can replace routing used by another application.
New setup uses the supported dashboard flow; the public import schema omits legacy credential fields.
A pending or uncertain import is not permission to use or re-import the number.

pages.title: Update number credentials or remove a connection
pages.description: Replace carrier credentials in place, preserve number settings and reconcile uncertain routing or removal without deleting and re-importing.
pages.lead: Replace a number’s carrier credentials in place, or remove its connection deliberately while tracking external routing cleanup.
important: Credential updates keep the existing number and its settings; they do not switch carrier.
Use one supported credential pair and keep the request private.
An uncertain routing or removal result requires reconciliation, not automatic replay.
